parse.title: The project list comes from GitHub, not from the pod's working tree

steps.text: repo:Remote
runs command:KitServe
reports origin:GitHub
today the list is readdirSync(behaviours/*.beh) against the checkout
the process happens to sit in — correct for a laptop, meaningless for a
pod whose clone is an implementation detail of its image

parse.title: A public project's behaviours are served without a token, on a request of their own

steps.text: project:Public
runs command:KitServe
reports auth:NotRequired
his instinct, quoted: "obviously beh from public repos dont need to be
authenticated so maybe can be returned faster" — so the split is not a
performance tweak layered on later, it is which credential the request needs
a public read that fails because a token could not be minted is a bug

parse.title: A private project is served only against a live installation token

steps.text: project:Private
runs command:KitServe
reports auth:InstallationToken
the kit-github secret he created on 2026-09-27 holds an app id, an
installation id and a private key — a credential that is EXCHANGED for a
short-lived token, never sent as one
an expired token is re-minted rather than returned as a failed read, which
is what he meant by "some similar refresh token mechanism to what you are using"

parse.title: The backend parses, resolves and generates; the frontend renders what it is handed

steps.text: request:Project
runs command:KitServe
reports work:ServerSide
"I am envisioning, the frontend has the UI, keep it light let the backend
do the heavy lifting" — so the generated test a screen shows is computed
server-side and arrives as data; the browser never carries the engine
this is also what makes the engine's language a private decision rather
than a public one

parse.title: A behaviour is added to a project from a phone

steps.text: opens page:KitHostedProject
sees button:KitHostedAddBehaviour
"top priority now I think is deploying kit so that I can use it from my
phone" — the phone is the requirement, not a nice-to-have, and it is why
nothing here may depend on a loopback bind

parse.title: An existing behaviour is updated without rewriting the file around it

steps.text: opens page:KitHostedBehaviour
sees button:KitHostedSave
writer.js already splices one block so every comment survives
(kit.beh BEH-WRITE-1); hosted Kit must keep that property, because the
headers in this directory are where a corpus's caveats live

parse.title: A behaviour is removed, and the removal is refused if anything still references it

steps.text: opens page:KitHostedBehaviour
sees button:KitHostedRemove
⚠️ THE ONLY ONE OF HIS THREE VERBS THAT HAS NO IMPLEMENTATION AT ALL —
writer.js can add a step and splice a block, and has no remove path
a behaviour can be the target of `serves` or `cites` from another one, so
deleting it silently is how a corpus acquires a dangling reference

parse.title: Edits are held until Commit, so a half-described change never reaches a branch

steps.text: opens page:KitHostedProject
sees button:KitHostedCommit

parse.asks: Does a hosted edit write to GitHub immediately, or accumulate until Commit?

options.label: Accumulate until Commit
options.consequence: the Commit button is the only thing that talks to GitHub; a change spanning three behaviours lands as one commit, and abandoning it costs nothing

options.label: Write each edit straight through
options.consequence: no server-side state at all, and the pod can die mid-change without losing anything; but every keystroke-level save is a commit, and a spec described over five edits arrives as five red branches

recommend.label: Accumulate until Commit
recommend.why: your own sentence puts Commit at the end of a list of edits — 'add new behaviours, update behaviours, remove behaviours etc and then can Commit' — which reads as a staging step. And a change is usually more than one behaviour: BEH-PULL-2 and BEH-PULL-3 above are one decision of yours described twice.

parse.against: Accumulating means the pod holds unsaved work, and you said there is no volume for it — a restart between your last edit and Commit loses the lot. Writing straight through cannot lose anything, and five small PRs are annoying rather than dangerous.

parse.title: Commit creates a branch off dev, and never a commit on dev

steps.text: change:Pending
runs command:KitCommit
reports branch:Created
answering the question mark in his own sentence: it has to be a branch
a spec written before its code exists makes check.js exit 1 BY DESIGN
(kit.beh BEH-GATE-1), so committing to dev would push a known-red tree
onto the branch every other PR is measured against
⚠️ UNBUILT: git-store.js defaults to `opts.branch || currentBranch(cwd)`,
so today a pod would push a phone edit onto whatever branch its clone sits on

parse.title: The commit is attributed to Kit, not to the person who pressed Commit

steps.text: change:Pending
runs command:KitCommit
reports author:Kit
his override on kit#88, 2026-09-30: "Let's let the commit belong to kit
for now… using the gh app speeds up timelines"
⚠️ THIS IS A TRADE HE MADE KNOWINGLY, NOT A LIMITATION — commit
attribution was the argument that carried the earlier web-flow decision,
and he judged shipping sooner worth more while Kit has one user
the condition for revisiting it is a SECOND USER, not a date

parse.title: A pull request is opened for the branch, because that is where the work is picked up

steps.text: branch:Pushed
runs command:KitCommit
reports pull:Opened
"Here the AI (you for now) can read the behaviour changes, update the
generated tests, update inferences etc, implement changes in the app to get
the tests passing - raise a PR"
the PR is the handover: a pushed branch with no PR is invisible to every
instrument that looks for work

parse.title: The branch a Commit produces is red, and the red is the work item

steps.text: branch:Pushed
runs command:KitCheck
exits status:One
MEASURED on 2026-09-30, on a throwaway copy of this corpus directory:
adding one unimplemented behaviour took `20/20 behaviour(s) have a test
naming them` to `20/21` and exit 0 to exit 1
so "the tests are failing" is the normal state of a fresh Kit branch, and
anything that treats a red branch as a fault will fight the workflow he
described rather than serve it

parse.title: A read is served to anyone, and that stays true in every configuration

steps.text: request:Anonymous
runs command:KitServe
reports status:Ok
kit is a public repo, so a corpus served to an unauthenticated caller
discloses nothing that `git clone` does not
gating reads would cost the thing he wants — glancing at a spec from a
phone — to protect data that is already public

parse.title: A write is refused unless the caller proved they are the operator

steps.text: request:Unauthenticated
runs command:KitCommit
reports status:Forbidden
this is the half BEH-WRITE-5 used to hold by binding loopback, which a
hosted service cannot do — so the gate moves from the interface to a
credential, and kit#47's KIT_PASSWORD is the first one
⚠️ TWO DIFFERENT LAYERS, and a later reader must not collapse them: the
App installation token is how KIT talks to GITHUB; the password is how a
PERSON is let into Kit. Neither substitutes for the other
